question: to the Commission Sandro Gozi (Renew), Damian Boeselager (Verts/ALE), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Hilde Vautmans (Renew), Hannes Heide (S&D), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Kim Van Sparrentak (Verts/ALE), Bernard Guetta (Renew), Sophie Wilmès (Renew), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Chloé Ridel (S&D), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Ciaran Mullooly (Renew), Irena Joveva (Renew), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Evin Incir (S&D) Subject:

According to Lakmusz, a Hungarian fact-checking website operating within the Hungarian Digital Media Observatory (HDMO), which is co-financed by the Commission, hundreds of sponsored ads have been used to spread AI‑generated political videos on Facebook in Hungary. These videos depict Hungarian soldiers being executed in scenes of warfare. At the same time, a fake website posing as an investigative media outlet has published a defamatory article targeting a public figure. That site has also been promoted through paid advertisements and visited by thousands of users. These pieces of content were shared in a pre-election period, with no indication as to who financed them. This casts doubt on whether the Digital Services Act (DSA) is being applied, particularly its provisions aimed at protecting the electoral process online. There are also concerns regarding the compliance of these activities with the European Regulation on the transparency and targeting of political advertising, which requires those who fund sponsored content to be clearly identified. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider the mass dissemination of such content to be in line with the obligations imposed on very large online platforms?
Has the Commission initiated or does it intend to initiate formal proceedings against Meta under the DSA?
What specific action does the Commission plan to take to guarantee that the EU rules effectively protect the integrity of democratic debate in the run-up to elections?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.6.2026) Under the Digital Services Act (DSA)1, very large online platforms (VLOPs) and very large online search engines are obliged to mitigate systemic risks to electoral processes. The Commission issued guidelines in this respect, which also cover political advertising and recommend measures such as labels for AI-generated content and technical detection measures2. Enforcing the DSA is a priority for the Commission. It has opened investigations concerning the compliance of Meta3 and TikTok4 with the DSA in the area of information integrity. As part of these ongoing investigations, the Commission is analysing reports related to incidents in Hungary. To enhance election preparedness, the Hungarian Digital Services Coordinator (DSC) hosted a DSA election roundtable on 5 March 2026 with VLOPs and national authorities to enhance election preparedness. The Commission attended upon invitation of the Hungarian DSC. Such roundtables have become best practice in preparing for national elections in Member States. In addition, from 2 August 2026, under the AI Act5, the duty to mark and enable detection when content, such as images, audio, or video, has been artificially generated or manipulated, and labelling of deep fakes and certain AI generated publications on public matters will apply. Looking ahead, under the European Democracy Shield6, the Commission is planning to develop a DSA incidents and crisis protocol to address major interference in the information environment and is working with the European Digital Services Board to update the election toolbox on election preparedness.
